c.tagline: Botswana's understated capital, gateway to safari country.

taxi.fareNote: Meters are used for short in-town trips; for longer journeys or airport transfers, agree the fare with the driver before departing.

emergency.note: 998 reaches the fire brigade; these toll-free numbers work from any phone, including mobiles.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Gaborone West (Grand Palm): Grand Palm Hotel Casino Convention Resort

avoid.reason: Avoid the Old Naledi township and walking anywhere in the city after dark.
Bag- and phone-snatching around the main bus rank and Main Mall; use taxis at night.

hood_desc: Gaborone's walkable government and business core around the pedestrian Main Mall, with banks, the stock exchange, and government offices. Suits business travelers and first-time visitors who want everything within walking distance.

A leafy, established diplomatic and residential district near the National Museum, known for owner-run guesthouses and quiet tree-lined streets. Suits travelers wanting a homely, low-key base close to the center.

A hotel-and-retail cluster built around Airport Junction Mall on the A1 just north of the CBD, minutes from Sir Seretse Khama International Airport. Suits transit travelers, early departures, and business visitors needing airport proximity.

Home to the sprawling Grand Palm casino-and-convention resort with pools, restaurants, and nightlife on the western edge of the city. Suits conference delegates, families, and travelers wanting resort-style amenities.
A quieter southern district at the foot of Kgale Hill, close to Mokolodi Nature Reserve and hiking trails. Suits nature-minded travelers and those breaking a journey to or from safari lodges.
lodging: Peermont Walmont at the Grand Palm
Peermont Metcourt Inn at the Grand Palm

water.note: Officially treated and chlorinated, but water-quality audits and rural inconsistencies mean bottled water is the safer choice.

transit.pay: Fares on buses and combis are paid in cash directly to the driver or conductor in Botswana Pula; there is no rechargeable transit card. Fares are flat-rate by route, so keep small change on hand.
transit.hours: Buses and combis generally operate from around 6am to 8pm with sparse Sunday service; there is little to no service after dark, so taxis or ride-hailing apps are needed at night.
transit.note: A limited Botswana Railways passenger line passes through Gaborone toward Lobatse and Francistown, but most residents and visitors rely on combis, buses, and taxis for getting around.

bus: Local combi minibuses and intercity coaches from the main bus rank

tip.r: Tipping is not deeply ingrained but is appreciated; round up or add roughly 10% at sit-down restaurants, and tip safari guides, drivers, and porters directly in cash.
